still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, and Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent obesity benefit.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling: 32.0% ever-used − 20.9% current = 11.1% of adults used and are off now. ~57% of current users are on a second or later course (11.9 pts) and 2.6 pts cycled and are off again, so 14.5 / 32.0 ≈ 45% of ever-users have cycled. The remaining 8.5 pts stopped once and have not restarted. This fits one-year persistence of ~one-third on brand weekly and oral products, ~38% on $39–69 generic semaglutide (fewer people stop over cost), ~60% on clinic MariTide inside tracks, and 36–47% restarting within a year. Age check (2032 weights): 0.20×12 + 0.33×21.5 + 0.24×30.5 + 0.23×18 = 2.4 + 7.1 + 7.3 + 4.1 ≈ 20.9. Income thirds average ~21.2 and bracket the national figure. 20.9% of ~274M adults ≈ 57.3M users. Payer mix: commercial ~12.4M (down from 13.9M as employer coverage fell), Medicare ~12.6M, Medicaid ~5.0M, legitimate cash ~23.3M (incl. ~11M on generic semaglutide, ~2.0M on calm plans, ~2.4M in employer verified-fill stipend programmes), gray/counterfeit ~4.0M (down from 7.5M as $39 domestic generics undercut mail-order). 12.4+12.6+5.0+23.3+4.0 = 57.3M. Most of the bottom third's gain (14 → 15.5) came from gray-market users switching to legal generic vials and from new conditioned Medicaid coverage. That makes it more legal than in 2032, but still the most conditional use in the country. Adult obesity ~32.9%. ~22% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the rural South, among uninsured men, and among 65+ adults without qualifying codes who distrust the vials. ~5.5M adults have used continuously for 5+ years, the population exposed to the new long-horizon signal. Pediatric: ~1.3% of under-18s are on a drug and ~2.9% of 12–17s, up because generic semaglutide is cheap for families. About 0.2% of 6–11s take liraglutide, down further after the EMA restriction. ~4.8M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~12.6M users) still reaches users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, plus alcohol use disorder since the Apr 2033 approval of oral semaglutide for AUD (~0.7M Medicare AUD users on the brand pill). Generic semaglutide is now preferred on most Part D formularies for diabetes and CV codes. FICTIONAL arithmetic: average Medicare net is ~0.35 × $45 (generic) + 0.65 × $235 (brands) ≈ $170 a month. 12.6M × $170 × 12 ≈ $25.7B a year, down from ~$31.6B in 2032 despite 1.4M more users. Within that, AUD is ~0.7M × ~$190 × 12 ≈ $1.6B. Medicaid: 12 states now cover weight-loss use (up from 7). Seven of them condition coverage on verified fills and quarterly weigh-ins: the two pre-existing programmes plus five 1115 waivers approved Feb 2034 (Georgia, Arkansas, Indiana, Oklahoma, Tennessee). ~5.0M Medicaid users × ~$70 average net × 12 ≈ $4.2B a year.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $4–30 a month and Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials $20–60. India and China still supply about two-thirds of world incretin volume and most of the API in US generic semaglutide. Canadian generics are now CAD 40–70.
access.note: FICTIONAL. US generic semaglutide injection entered Apr 2033 under the Feb 2033 patent settlement (Viatris, Teva, Sandoz, Dr. Reddy's, plus a Novo authorised generic). By early 2034 there were seven ANDA holders. Cash prices are $39–49 for multi-dose vials and $59–69 for generic pens. Brand repricing: MariTide cash $249 → $199. Zepbound/Mounjaro TrumpRx $199–249. Wegovy pill maintenance $169 (starting doses still $149). Foundayo $129–199. Retatrutide list still $1,299, ~$349 cash direct. No generic tirzepatide, oral semaglutide or orforglipron exists. The two-tier split is now formal. Covered workers (~12.4M commercial, ~6.8M of them in monitored tracks, ~4.6M on clinic MariTide; ~5.3M MariTide users in total) get brand weekly or monthly products with coaching and DXA. The uncovered majority injects $41 generic vials. ~29% of large employers that dropped coverage instead pay $25–50 a month stipends for app-verified generic fills (~2.4M employees). The US cash-to-Indian-generic gap fell from ~40–50× to ~2–5×, so gray use (~4.0M) is now mainly tirzepatide and retatrutide analogues, plus people without a prescriber or without documents. Orals are ~48% of users.

GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)

Activin type II receptor antibody, lean-mass adjunct (bimagrumab, approved Jul 2033 for adults 60+ on incretin therapy at sarcopenia risk)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral parity is realised by readout and filing, not approval. Novo's oral amycretin phase 3 (Sep 2033) showed 20.6% weight loss at 72 weeks, non-inferior to an injectable tirzepatide arm at 20.9%. The NDA was filed Jan 2034 under standard review, with an FDA action date in Q1 2035, so the drug is not on the US market at the end of 2034. Under the envelope rules a product absent from the 2032 pipeline cannot be approved here. Physicians and investors already price in a needle-free pill at tirzepatide efficacy, and some employer tracks have deferred MariTide contract renewals. Oral semaglutide for AUD was approved Apr 2033 after a major-amendment extension. Bimagrumab (filed Jul 2032) was approved Jul 2033 at ~$900/month list with ~0.3M users, mostly in premium tracks. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial read out Sep 2034, consistent in the CVD population; Lilly has not resubmitted for non-CVD adults, and resubmission is expected no earlier than 2035 with a fracture-mitigation plan. Implants remain phase 1–2. No generic tirzepatide before 2036 patent expiry. Global incretin revenue is ~$152B (2033), down from ~$165B on falling semaglutide prices despite higher volume.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Self-titration errors with generic multi-dose vials have added a wave of first-month vomiting among new cash users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; gastroparesis caution retained; generic vial labelling carries a syringe-unit dosing chart.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation centres on EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; EPI MDL ongoing, first bellwether set for 2035.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after more than 2 years, ~1.45 after three or more cycles. Bimagrumab is approved for lean mass, with no fracture-outcome data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; DXA code in use; bimagrumab label states no fracture benefit has been shown.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults, including in the Sentinel psychiatric study.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening while on drug
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: the FDA Sentinel postmarketing study (Nov 2033) confirmed dose-related clinically meaningful anhedonia: ~7% of users vs ~3% of matched controls, ~10% on retatrutide, ~4% at calm-plan microdoses. Most users still report only mild evenness.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 'Anhedonia and reduced interest' added to adverse reactions across the class (Jan 2034). Untitled letters to calm platforms continued; no rule followed.

safety_ledger.effect: Persistent anhedonia after discontinuation in users with 5+ years of continuous exposure ('protracted flatness')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL, NEW. In Sentinel and a Danish registry replication, adults who stopped after 5+ years of continuous semaglutide or tirzepatide had anhedonia persisting 6+ months after their last dose at ~4.8%. The rate was ~2.0% in those who stopped after under 2 years and ~1.6% in regain-matched non-users who stopped other weight treatments (adjusted HR ~2.3). A 48-person PET substudy found lower striatal dopamine synthesis capacity in affected users. The signal did not appear in trials of up to 4 years. Confounders: depression unmasked by regain, and the selection of who stays on 5 years. ~5.5M Americans are in the exposed group.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Nov 2033). Postmarketing requirement for a randomised taper-versus-continuation study. EMA PRAC review opened. No boxed warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; underpins chronic-therapy framing and adherence monitoring.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency. Low ferritin in adolescent girls is rising with cheap generic starts.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language on labels.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~2× incidence after 5+ years of semaglutide. Tirzepatide's excess is now nominally significant in one cohort (HR ~1.4).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling (2031), carried to all generic labels. Tirzepatide review continues.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; decades-long pediatric exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The first post-discontinuation psychiatric signal arrived in 2033 (see the protracted-flatness entry). Cycling effects on bone, pancreas and reward remain poorly characterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric growth PMRs continue; taper study required.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: no new multistate infection cluster since 2031. Poison-centre calls are down ~30% from 2032 peak but now include legal generic-vial syringe errors. Super-potent Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials still cause ED visits.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts maintained; no statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: 36-month liraglutide PMR data show height velocity ~0.6 cm/year below expected with partial catch-up after stopping. The Swedish ARFID HR is ~1.8. Final adult height is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA growth monitoring label. EMA restricted initiation under 12 to specialist centres (2033). AAP lifestyle-first guidance. No FDA age restriction.

food_and_beverage.state: ~39% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~12% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~11%. Dollar sales slipped ~1% in 2033 as premium mix stopped offsetting volume. Generic access in lower-income zip codes cut the regain-driven value-pack demand Kroger and Albertsons had planned around. Private-label 'half-pack' formats are now the fastest-growing SKUs. Pea protein supply eased.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~16% from 2025 and beer ~10%. The on-label AUD approval and $41 off-label generics hit heavy drinkers, who make up most of the volume. Treatment programmes and EAPs prescribe routinely. Brown-Forman and Constellation cut US distillery and brewery shifts; Midwestern tavern closures continue. Non-alcoholic drinks are ~3% of volume.

restaurants.state: Half portions are the default order at Darden and Brinker chains, and a 'full' portion is now an upsell. QSR value-menu growth slowed in Memphis-type markets as users switched from gray vials to steady generic supply. Bar-and-grill formats are contracting.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep consolidating. Mass retailers now set size runs by zip code. Regainer resale and stretch lines continue. Structured athleticwear and tailoring grow in the upper tier.

fitness.state: Strength training grows. Bimagrumab is now a premium add-on at DXA-coaching clinics. Budget chains bundle $39 lean-mass sessions with pharmacy generic pickup kiosks. Family strength gyms continue to gain.

insurance.state: Employer weight-loss coverage is down to 24%. Commercial pharmacy trend fell to ~+3% as generic semaglutide substitution took hold. Covered employers keep brand access inside monitored tracks. Uncovered employers pay verified-fill stipends, which cost less than a benefit. Part D premiums rose only modestly in 2034 because Medicare's incretin spend fell.

pharma.state: Novo's US semaglutide revenue fell roughly half after generic entry. It paid the $2.4B DOJ settlement and is betting on oral amycretin. Lilly holds share on tirzepatide, which has no generic until 2036, and on Foundayo. Amgen's MariTide growth slowed as employers wait for the pill. Viatris, Teva and Indian generic makers gained most in US volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being medicated no longer signals anything, because nearly everyone is. What reads is the product. A lifted body with a DXA print means covered brand or pill. Thin with vial bruises on the thigh means generic cash. Thin with a monthly clinic bruise means a track. Regained after 50 now prompts a question rather than a class judgement: why are you off?
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle and 'off-drug lean' remain the elite markers in Charlotte and Austin, though after the Nov 2033 communication the off-drug boast is less often aimed at people who have been on for 7 years. On the Columbus freight corridor, workers whose employers dropped coverage now inject $41 generic semaglutide and log the vial into a stipend app. In Memphis the visible body changed: the cycler's face is rarer, and TennCare's weigh-in day at the FQHC is a monthly ritual. Upper-income parents still keep prepubertal children off, while generic starts in teenagers rose fastest in households that a family doctor reaches more easily than a specialist.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are short and protein-forward. A full plate at a work lunch draws comment. Bread Alone claims ~700 congregations. School debates centre on whether nurses should log students' generic fills for parents.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps dropped the 'on a calm plan' tag because it no longer distinguished anyone. Some added 'off since' as a field. Being off for good reasons (pregnancy, EPI, a taper) is explained up front, the way people once explained not drinking.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has become something people account for. Saying 'I'm hungry' at work sounds like a disclosure. Unmuted reframed itself around long-term users who are afraid to stop, while fat-acceptance revivalists and MAHA stay separate.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Sentinel puts clinically meaningful on-drug anhedonia at ~7% of users (~4M people), ~10% on retatrutide and ~4% at calm microdoses. A new long-horizon signal: ~4.8% of people who stop after 5+ continuous years remain flat 6+ months later. ~2.0M calm-plan subscribers and ~9.2M workers under some form of adherence verification (6.8M in tracks, 2.4M in stipend programmes).
interior_life.framing: Employers call it 'steadiness' and pay for proof of it. Platforms say 'quiet' and, since the settlement, never name a brand. Clinicians and the label now call it anhedonia. Long-term users call the new finding 'the lock-in'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Workforce-scheduling software at two national call-centre operators and several Columbus-corridor 3PLs counts track or stipend enrollment as a 'reliability' input. A Jun 2034 NBER working paper found enrollees 18% less likely to separate within a year, much of it selection. Job postings in logistics now list 'wellness track participation preferred'. The EEOC issued right-to-sue letters in 2033, and one ADA suit (Doe v. Tellus Contact Solutions) is pending in the Southern District of Ohio. FMCSA guidance (Jun 2034) says prescribed AUD use does not disqualify commercial drivers and leaves calm use to medical examiners.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir gave way to 'taper' memoir: long-term users afraid that stopping won't bring feeling back. Unmuted's off nights in Detroit, Baltimore and Memphis now include taper support circles. Ambient TV keeps growing. Sportsbook handle per active account fell again. Bar trivia leagues in Ohio merged as taverns closed.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples where one partner wants to taper and the other prefers them steady now make up a recognisable caseload in couples practices. Desire mismatch remains the leading complaint. The partner who is off is more often described as 'a lot'.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The Senate HELP hearing on Novo's calm-platform payments produced bipartisan anger and no bill. The National Health Law Program sued over Georgia's conditioned Medicaid waiver. Midterm candidates in both parties claimed the $41 generic. California and New York adherence-premium bans died in committee, so Illinois remains alone. MAHA legislators added the teenage generic data to the children's hearings.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive and procedural. FDA approved generic semaglutide (after the settlement), the AUD indication and bimagrumab, accepted the oral amycretin NDA, issued the protracted-flatness DSC and added anhedonia to labels. It enforced against nothing new in calm marketing; DOJ did that through the Novo settlement.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No federal subsidy. CMS approved five 1115 waivers (Feb 2034) adding generic semaglutide for obesity, conditioned on verified fills and quarterly weigh-ins, with coverage suspended after two missed verifications. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Generic vials carry lot QR codes that stipend apps and Medicaid PBMs scan to verify fills. FQHC weigh-ins feed state Medicaid dashboards. Clinic administration records still flow to wellness vendors. Calm platforms still sell de-identified mood cohorts. Some Ohio and Texas county DUI courts accept adherence-verified semaglutide alongside existing monitoring.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE covers the AUD indication. The Army oral recruit pilot continues unexpanded. FMCSA AUD guidance issued; calm use left to examiners.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: US generic semaglutide relies on Indian and Chinese API, so the FDA now inspects some of the same plants it once named in import alerts. US–India talks shifted from mail enforcement to API quality agreements. Chinese tirzepatide analogues remain the main gray import.

events.event: Novo Nordisk settles semaglutide formulation-patent litigation; FDA approves generic semaglutide injection from Viatris, Teva, Sandoz and Dr. Reddy's with April entry, and by March 2034 multi-dose vials sell for $39–49 cash
FDA approves oral semaglutide to reduce heavy drinking days in adults with alcohol use disorder; ASAM's October guideline lists it first-line where metabolic disease coexists

FDA Sentinel study and a Danish registry find people who stop after five or more continuous years are about twice as likely to stay anhedonic six months later; FDA issues a safety communication and orders a taper trial
Novo files oral amycretin after a phase 3 readout matching injectable tirzepatide at ~21% weight loss; FDA sets a Q1 2035 action date

CMS approves five state Medicaid waivers adding generic semaglutide for obesity only for enrollees who verify fills and weigh in quarterly, mirroring the stipend model employers adopted as coverage fell to 24%

events.event: Novo Nordisk pays $2.4 billion to settle DOJ claims that it paid telehealth 'calm' platforms per-prescription 'adherence support' fees to promote off-label use, and accepts a five-year corporate integrity agreement

open_tensions: About 5.5 million Americans have been on continuously for five or more years, and the new signal suggests stopping may not bring feeling back for some of them. Their employers, their Medicaid programmes and their partners all reward staying on, and the taper trial will not report before 2037.

The drug now costs $41, and access depends on whether you scan the vial. Seven state Medicaid programmes and ~9 million workers verify adherence, the Georgia lawsuit is pending, and Illinois is still the only state with a ban.
Oral amycretin's 2035 decision will put tirzepatide-level efficacy in a branded pill that covered workers will get and generic-vial users will not, while MariTide contracts wait on it.
Teenage generic starts are rising in households with the least specialist monitoring, while the growth and protracted-flatness data are both about long exposure that started young.

prose.headline: Off It? Explain Yourself. Semaglutide Costs $41 Now, and Your Employer Would Like to See the Receipt
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 about one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, some fifty-seven million people, and almost a third have tried one. The share rose only a point and a bit in two years, even as the price fell through the floor. In April 2033, after Novo Nordisk settled its last patent fight, generic semaglutide reached pharmacies. A multi-dose vial now costs about forty dollars. The box of branded Wegovy still says $1,349, and nobody pays it.

The cheap vial did not so much add users as move them. Millions who had bought Indian vials or cloned pens through Telegram now buy legal generics at the counter, and the gray market has shrunk to the people chasing tirzepatide copies and the people no prescriber reaches. With price no longer the barrier, the question became who pays, and on what terms. Only about a quarter of employers still cover the drugs for weight. Many of the rest pay a small monthly stipend instead, cheaper than a benefit, and release it when an app confirms the fill. Covered workers get brand pills, monthly clinic shots and muscle scans. Everyone else gets the vial and the app. In February 2034 five states won federal permission to add the generic to Medicaid for obesity, but only for enrollees who verify their fills and step on a scale every quarter. Miss two checks and the coverage pauses.

On the work floor this barely registers as policy. Scheduling software at call centres and freight warehouses near Columbus counts wellness-track enrolment as a reliability signal. Job ads say participation is preferred. An economics paper found enrollees less likely to leave or be let go, and could not say how much of that was the drug and how much was the kind of person who enrolls. A disability lawsuit is moving slowly through a federal court in Ohio.

In April 2033 the FDA approved oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder, and addiction doctors put it beside naltrexone. Spirits sales are down about a sixth from 2025. Heavy drinkers, who drove the volume, are the people the drug reaches best, and many of them use the forty-dollar generic off-label rather than the branded pill.

The news that changed the mood came in November 2033. An FDA surveillance study confirmed that the drugs dull pleasure in a minority of users, and found something no trial had run long enough to see. Among people who stopped after five or more continuous years, about one in twenty stayed flat six months later, roughly twice the rate of shorter-term users. A small brain-imaging study pointed at dopamine. The confounders are real: regain is depressing, and those who stay on five years are not a random group. The FDA ordered a taper trial that will take years. Long-term users call it the lock-in. Nobody can yet say whether it is real, and some are afraid to find out.

In May Novo paid $2.4 billion to settle charges that it had quietly paid telehealth calm platforms per prescription. The platforms switched to generics and kept growing. Two million people now subscribe. Novo's hope is a pill: oral amycretin matched injectable tirzepatide in its final trial and awaits a decision early next year, at a brand price.

On a Charlotte office floor or a Memphis clinic queue, nobody remarks on who is on it. Half portions are the default at chain restaurants. Dating apps dropped the calm-plan tag because everyone has it. What draws a question now is being off, and people who are off explain it the way non-drinkers once explained a soda at the bar. Teenagers are starting the generic through family doctors more often than through specialists. Their growth charts are filled in less often than their pharmacy records.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Renee Okafor's alarm goes at 4:40. Sunday is shot day, but she does it Monday now, so the app catches it before the stipend window closes. She draws twelve units from the vial, pinches the left thigh, and holds the QR code under the phone until it chimes green. Forty-one dollars at Kroger, forty back from Meridian Freight on the fifteenth.

At the Groveport dock she checks the board. Her name sits in the blue column, reliable, next to two new hires who aren't enrolled yet. She doesn't say anything to them. Somebody will.

Lunch is half a chicken wrap in the break room. Marcus from receiving eats a whole one, and Tasha asks him, friendly, if he's off. He says his doctor's tapering him for the pancreas thing. Everyone nods. That's an acceptable answer.

At three her sister texts from Memphis. Weigh-in at the clinic went fine, TennCare stays on. A thumbs-up.

She drives home past the Polish bar that closed. Her husband, Dele, is at the stove making jollof, the full pot, the way his mother did. He went off in March. He laughs louder now. He cried at a car commercial last week and seemed pleased about it.

She eats a small plate. He watches her eat it.

After the kids are down she reads the FDA thing again on her phone, the part about five years. She started in 2027. She counts on her fingers and stops.

Dele asks if she wants to try stopping, just to see.

"After the review," she says. "In the spring." She turns off the lamp. The phone chimes green, a reminder for next week.
